# Every user with their email, if any.
users = SQL[tuple[int, str, str | None]]("""--sql
SELECT id, name, email FROM users""")
sources.joins:
import decimal
from sqlty import SQL

# Each order repeats once per item, so AVG(o.total) weighs it by its item count.
segment_totals = SQL[tuple[str, decimal.Decimal, decimal.Decimal]]("""--sql
SELECT c.segment, AVG(o.total) AS avg_order, SUM(i.amount) AS revenue
FROM orders o
JOIN customers c ON c.id = o.customer_id
JOIN order_items i ON i.order_id = o.id
GROUP BY c.segment""")

# Aggregated per order first: one row per order, no warning.
segment_totals_fixed = SQL[tuple[str, decimal.Decimal, decimal.Decimal]]("""--sql
WITH items AS (
    SELECT order_id, SUM(amount) AS amount FROM order_items GROUP BY order_id
)
SELECT c.segment, AVG(o.total) AS avg_order, SUM(i.amount) AS revenue
FROM orders o
JOIN customers c ON c.id = o.customer_id
JOIN items i ON i.order_id = o.id
GROUP BY c.segment""")

# Items and payments both join orders one-to-many: each repeats the other.
order_balance = SQL[tuple[int, decimal.Decimal, decimal.Decimal]]("""--sql
SELECT o.id, SUM(i.amount) AS billed, SUM(p.amount) AS paid
FROM orders o
JOIN order_items i ON i.order_id = o.id
JOIN payments p ON p.order_id = o.id
GROUP BY o.id""")

# products.id holds products keys, orders.customer_id customers keys.
wrong_key = SQL[tuple[str, int]]("""--sql
SELECT p.name, o.id
FROM orders o
JOIN products p ON p.id = o.customer_id""")

questions.question: How many users are there?
questions.problem: The board asks how big our user base is.
questions.gold: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM users

questions.question: Names of the users without an email.
questions.problem: We can't send receipts to users who never gave us an email, so support has to call them by name.
questions.gold: SELECT name FROM users WHERE email IS NULL

questions.question: Total revenue of all orders.
questions.problem: Finance needs our all-time revenue for the annual report.
questions.gold: SELECT SUM(total) FROM orders

questions.question: Each user's name and number of orders, including users with no orders.
questions.problem: To spot inactive accounts we look at how many orders each user has placed, and users who never ordered count too.
questions.gold: SELECT u.name, COUNT(o.id) FROM users AS u LEFT JOIN orders AS o ON o.user_id = u.id GROUP BY u.id, u.name

questions.question: The 5 users who spent the most, with how much they spent.
questions.problem: We want to thank our 5 biggest spenders and mention how much each of them spent.
questions.gold: SELECT u.name, SUM(o.total) AS spent FROM users AS u JOIN orders AS o ON o.user_id = u.id GROUP BY u.id, u.name ORDER BY spent DESC LIMIT 5

questions.question: Ids and totals of the orders placed in 2025.
questions.problem: Accounting is closing the 2025 books and needs every order from that year with its total.
questions.gold: SELECT id, total FROM orders WHERE placed_at >= '2025-01-01' AND placed_at < '2026-01-01'

questions.question: Average order total per user name.
questions.problem: We suspect some users place small orders and others large ones, so we compare the typical order total of each user by name.
questions.gold: SELECT u.name, AVG(o.total) FROM users AS u JOIN orders AS o ON o.user_id = u.id GROUP BY u.id, u.name

questions.question: Names of the users who never placed an order.
questions.problem: Marketing wants to send a first-purchase coupon to users who have signed up but never ordered.
questions.gold: SELECT name FROM users AS u WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM orders AS o WHERE o.user_id = u.id)

questions.question: Each user's name with the time of their latest order.
questions.problem: To find users who went quiet, we check when each user last ordered.
questions.gold: SELECT u.name, MAX(o.placed_at) FROM users AS u JOIN orders AS o ON o.user_id = u.id GROUP BY u.id, u.name

questions.question: Number of orders per month.
questions.problem: We're planning warehouse staffing and need to see how order volume changes month by month.
questions.gold: SELECT date_trunc('month', placed_at) AS month, COUNT(*) FROM orders GROUP BY 1

questions.question: Users whose email ends with @example.com.
questions.problem: example.com is shutting down its mail service, so we have to warn the users with an address there.
questions.gold: SELECT * FROM users WHERE email LIKE '%@example.com'

questions.question: The largest order's total and the name of the user who placed it.
questions.problem: Our record order deserves a shout-out: how much was it, and who placed it?
questions.gold: SELECT o.total, u.name FROM orders AS o JOIN users AS u ON u.id = o.user_id ORDER BY o.total DESC LIMIT 1

questions.question: Total order value per customer segment.
questions.problem: Sales wants to know which customer segment brings in the most order value.
questions.gold: SELECT c.segment, SUM(o.total) FROM customers AS c JOIN orders AS o ON o.customer_id = c.id GROUP BY c.segment

questions.question: Number of customers in each segment.
questions.problem: Before re-segmenting, we need to know how many customers sit in each segment.
questions.gold: SELECT segment, COUNT(*) FROM customers GROUP BY segment

questions.question: For every product, how many order items it has, including products never ordered.
questions.problem: We're pruning the catalog and need each product's number of order items, with zero for products nobody ordered.
questions.gold: SELECT p.name, COUNT(oi.id) FROM products AS p LEFT JOIN order_items AS oi ON oi.product_id = p.id GROUP BY p.id, p.name

questions.question: The 3 products with the highest revenue from order items.
questions.problem: We want to promote our 3 best-selling products by revenue from order items.
questions.gold: SELECT p.name, SUM(oi.amount) AS revenue FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON oi.product_id = p.id GROUP BY p.id, p.name ORDER BY revenue DESC LIMIT 3

questions.question: Ids of the orders that have no payments.
questions.problem: Collections is chasing orders nobody has paid anything for yet.
questions.gold: SELECT o.id FROM orders AS o WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM payments AS p WHERE p.order_id = o.id)

questions.question: Ids of the orders whose payments add up to less than the order total.
questions.problem: Some orders are only partly paid; we need the ones whose payments don't cover the order total.
questions.gold: SELECT o.id FROM orders AS o JOIN payments AS p ON p.order_id = o.id GROUP BY o.id, o.total HAVING SUM(p.amount) < o.total

questions.question: Average number of items per order.
questions.problem: Fulfilment is sizing boxes and wants to know how many items a typical order has.
questions.gold: SELECT AVG(n) FROM (SELECT COUNT(oi.id) AS n FROM orders AS o LEFT JOIN order_items AS oi ON oi.order_id = o.id GROUP BY o.id) AS t

questions.question: Ids of the customers who bought the product named 'Widget'.
questions.problem: The Widget has a recall, so we have to contact every customer who bought one.
questions.gold: SELECT DISTINCT o.customer_id FROM orders AS o JOIN order_items AS oi ON oi.order_id = o.id JOIN products AS p ON p.id = oi.product_id WHERE p.name = 'Widget'

questions.question: Emails of the users who placed at least one order over 500.
questions.problem: We want to invite users who have placed a big order, over 500, to our VIP program by email.
questions.gold: SELECT DISTINCT u.email FROM users AS u JOIN orders AS o ON o.user_id = u.id WHERE o.total > 500

questions.question: Number of users without an email.
questions.problem: We're estimating how much of our user base we can't reach by email.
questions.gold: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM users WHERE email IS NULL

questions.question: Ids and dates of the 10 most recent orders.
questions.problem: Support wants a quick look at the 10 latest orders and when they came in.
questions.gold: SELECT id, placed_at FROM orders ORDER BY placed_at DESC LIMIT 10

questions.question: Average order total.
questions.problem: Pricing wants the average order total across the whole shop.
questions.gold: SELECT AVG(total) FROM orders

questions.question: Names of the users with more than 10 orders, with their order count.
questions.problem: Our loyalty tier is for users with more than 10 orders, and we want to show each one their order count.
questions.gold: SELECT u.name, COUNT(*) FROM users AS u JOIN orders AS o ON o.user_id = u.id GROUP BY u.id, u.name HAVING COUNT(*) > 10

questions.question: Total spent per user name in 2024, for users who ordered that year.
questions.problem: For 2024's year-in-review email, each user who ordered that year should see how much they spent.
questions.gold: SELECT u.name, SUM(o.total) FROM users AS u JOIN orders AS o ON o.user_id = u.id WHERE o.placed_at >= '2024-01-01' AND o.placed_at < '2025-01-01' GROUP BY u.id, u.name

questions.question: The smallest and the largest order total.
questions.problem: To set shipping tiers, we need the range of order totals, from the cheapest to the most expensive.
questions.gold: SELECT MIN(total), MAX(total) FROM orders

questions.question: Names of the users who ordered in both 2024 and 2025.
questions.problem: We want to reward users who came back: those who ordered in 2024 and again in 2025.
questions.gold: SELECT name FROM users WHERE id IN (SELECT user_id FROM orders WHERE placed_at >= '2024-01-01' AND placed_at < '2025-01-01') AND id IN (SELECT user_id FROM orders WHERE placed_at >= '2025-01-01' AND placed_at < '2026-01-01')

questions.question: Names of the products that were never ordered.
questions.problem: Some products have never sold and we want to drop them from the catalog.
questions.gold: SELECT name FROM products AS p WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM order_items AS i WHERE i.product_id = p.id)

questions.question: Revenue from order items per product name.
questions.problem: Merchandising needs to see how much revenue from order items each product name earns.
questions.gold: SELECT p.name, SUM(i.amount) FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS i ON i.product_id = p.id GROUP BY p.id, p.name

questions.question: Number of orders per customer segment.
questions.problem: We want to know which segment orders most often, by counting orders per segment.
questions.gold: SELECT c.segment, COUNT(o.id) FROM customers AS c JOIN orders AS o ON o.customer_id = c.id GROUP BY c.segment

questions.question: Total paid per order id, for orders with payments.
questions.problem: Accounting is reconciling payments and needs how much was paid on each order that has payments.
questions.gold: SELECT order_id, SUM(amount) FROM payments GROUP BY order_id

questions.question: Ids of the orders with more than 2 items.
questions.problem: Orders with more than 2 items ship in a bigger box, so the warehouse needs their ids.
questions.gold: SELECT order_id FROM order_items GROUP BY order_id HAVING COUNT(*) > 2

questions.question: Ids of the enterprise customers with their number of orders, including customers without orders.
questions.problem: Account managers handle enterprise customers and want each one's order count, including those who haven't ordered yet.
questions.gold: SELECT c.id, COUNT(o.id) FROM customers AS c LEFT JOIN orders AS o ON o.customer_id = c.id WHERE c.segment = 'enterprise' GROUP BY c.id

questions.question: Average order total per customer segment.
questions.problem: We're comparing segments by how large their orders are on average.
questions.gold: SELECT c.segment, AVG(o.total) FROM customers AS c JOIN orders AS o ON o.customer_id = c.id GROUP BY c.segment

questions.question: Number of distinct products each customer id bought.
questions.problem: To measure catalog breadth, we want to know how many different products each customer has bought.
questions.gold: SELECT o.customer_id, COUNT(DISTINCT i.product_id) FROM orders AS o JOIN order_items AS i ON i.order_id = o.id GROUP BY o.customer_id
